messages:
Emma (Product): quick sync — Customer X just asked for an embeddings endpoint that can accept large CSV uploads and return NDJSON/CSV. Their ask: up to 10k vectors per job, 1024 dims, sync UX if possible. Need decision on launch scope and SLA.

Rajesh (Eng-Platform): 10k synchronous is pretty heavy for hosted. Memory + latency spikes. We should differentiate hosted vs Dedicated. Hosted default limit I'd suggest 1,024 vectors per request, Dedicated can be bumped (configurable). Also need payload-size cap (eg 8MB) and streaming.

Kai (Eng-ML): model side — recommend shipping with two models: redwood-embed-medium (1024d) + redwood-embed-small (512d). redwood-embed-large (2048d) can be added later. For large batches consider chunking server-side and streaming partial NDJSON to the client.

Maya (Customer Success): Customer X's priority: end-user latency for small batches (<=64 vectors) under 300ms, plus ability to upload big exports. They prefer sync flow for the developer experience but will accept async for 10k. They asked for example CSVs in docs.

Emma (Product): Proposed MVP scope: hosted API supports sync up to 1,024 vectors/request, dims 512 & 1024, default response format NDJSON (one embedding per line). Document chunking strategy for >1,024 and provide an async job API for bulk imports. Launch criteria: API + SDK examples, perf metrics (64/256/1024), CS signoff, and cost-per-1k estimate. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Rajesh (Eng-Platform): +1 to hosted 1,024 default. Implementation notes: add server-side streaming via transfer-encoding chunking with Content-Type: application/x-ndjson; enforce per-request payload max 8MB (can surface different limits per tier). For Dedicated, we can expose a "max_vectors" config. Also we should add a `response_format` param: `ndjson` (default) and `base64` (opt-in) for compact transport.

Kai (Eng-ML): about `base64` — storing floats as base64 reduces payload but client work gets harder. I'd prefer arrays of floats as default to keep onboarding simple; offer `compress=true`/base64 for heavy customers. Also add eval docs: semantic-similarity delta between 512/1024/2048.

Emma (Product): decision lean: default arrays-of-floats in NDJSON, `response_format=base64` opt-in; hosted limit 1,024 vectors; offer async bulk job + CSV import tool. For launch we need: API (openapi + SDK updates), docs with CSV & NDJSON examples, migration notes, perf benchmarks, and a quick migration guide for customers moving from 512->1024 dims. Also add a note in pricing page: approximate cost per 1k vectors for each model.

Maya (Customer Success): Customer X says they'll accept hosted 1,024 as initial release if we provide a low-friction async path for 10k and a clear cost estimate. They also want CSV example and sample code for streaming NDJSON. :thumbsup:

Rajesh (Eng-Platform): I'll run perf runs on hosted infra for 64/256/1024 vectors across medium/small models and return latency + p99 + cost/1k in 48h. Will prototype streaming NDJSON and server-side chunking (chunk_size default 512). Also will add request-level `max_vectors` enforcement and helpful error messages (eg: 413 with suggested chunking code snippet).

Kai (Eng-ML): I'll prepare evaluation reports comparing 512/1024 quality on our standard semantic search prompt set and include guidance on which dims to pick by workload. Also will test quantized variants and note quality tradeoffs.

Emma (Product): Great — next steps: Rajesh (perf + implementation plan), Kai (eval + model recommendations), Maya (customer comms + migration checklist). Goal: ship non-enterprise MVP in 3 sprints, Dedicated/configurable limits later. Add ticket for `response_format` + streaming + async bulk. Thanks all.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: none — note for tracking, add a follow-up in #eng-releases when infra PRs land.

Emma (Product): tagging decision summary: hosted default 1,024 vectors, dims 512/1024, NDJSON arrays by default, base64 opt-in, async job API for >1,024. Launch criteria listed above. @Rajesh @Kai please confirm timelines.
